messages.subject: Re: Ask for help
messages.body_plain:
Hi Zhang -- thanks for the question.  It looks like you've gotten something out of order in the script.

SHORT VERSION:

Run this script, EXACTLY:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

MEDIUM VERSION:

After getting the example script to work, then copy and paste this exact script to a text file, and modify just the working directory, names of the tree and geog files, etc., to run your own data.

LONG VERSION

You cannot use "resDEC$outputs", specifically:

resDEC$outputs@params_table["d","init"]
resDEC$outputs@params_table["d","est"]

...until the Maximum Likelihood (ML) optimization is run.

If you have a desired start value for the parameter "d", you can just put it in directly:

========================
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["d","init"] = 0.05
========================

...or...

========================
dstart = 0.05
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["d","init"] = dstart
========================

I have "dstart" in some scripts because the idea is to take the ML estimate from a simpler model (like DEC) and use it as a starting point for optimization of a model complex model (like DEC+J).  But obviously this won't work for the simplest model (DEC).

Cheers,
Nick

PS: The lines that run the optimization are:

===============
res = bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)
res

save(res, file=resfn)
resDEC = res
===============

The object "resDEC" does not exist until this happens.
Cheers, Nick

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

Searching my hard drive -- I see that error came up once when I tried to read a NEXUS-format phylogeny via read.tree().

Nick

Uz
messages.body_snippet:
Dear Nick,
I'm wondering about ranges, how many regions or ranges could easy be handle in BioGeoBEARS for a big dataset (around 1000 species)?
Thank you,
Best,
Uz

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Ranges/regions
messages.body_plain:
Hi -- the likelihood calculations are:

- linear in the number of species (so twice as many species = about twice
as long to run)
- but they are exponential or worse in the number of ranges

- the number of ranges increases at:
number of ranges = number of states = 2^number_of_areas

Basically, you want to have fewer than about 1200 states/ranges. If you
have really big computers with dozens of cores it can be pushed up to about
2000 states/ranges, but it gets reeealy slow.

If you lower the maximum number of areas per range, you can increase the
total number of areas considered. See the example script, which reads:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script
####################################################
####################################################
# KEY HINT: The number of states (= number of different possible geographic
ranges)
# depends on (a) the number of areas and (b) max_range_size.
# If you have more than about 500-600 states, the calculations will get
REALLY slow,
# since the program has to exponentiate a matrix of e.g. 600x600.  Often
the computer
# will just sit there and crunch, and never get through the calculation of
the first
# likelihood.
#
# (this is also what is usually happening when LAGRANGE hangs: you have too
many states!)
#
# To check the number of states for a given number of ranges, try:
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=4, include_null_range=TRUE)
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=4, include_null_range=FALSE)
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=3, include_null_range=TRUE)
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=2, include_null_range=TRUE)

# Large numbers of areas have problems:
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=10, maxareas=10, include_null_range=TRUE)

# ...unless you limit the max_range_size:
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=10, maxareas=2, include_null_range=TRUE)
####################################################
####################################################

For 1000 species, I would try to keep it under 1000 states/ranges usually.

See also:

1. Question: Too many areas / too many states / BioGeoBEARS too slow.
Answers: diverse
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#too_many_areas

2. Get your list of ranges/states, from your list of areas
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#list_of_ranges

Cheers,
Nick

messages.subject: Automatically identifying nodes where specific evens occur
messages.subject_clean: Automatically identifying nodes where specific evens occur
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I'm trying to get my head around extracting data from results objects. In my study, I have a genus with species spread across a set of islands. I'm specifically interested in questions like is the average age of colonisation from A->B older than B->A. For a single tree this is easy, I can plot my tree with the best biogeographic estimation, figure out which nodes have the desired state change and just use prt() to get the ages of nodes I want. The trick is that I want to do this across a tree sample with changing node numbers to incorporate age variation of estimated trees. Does anybody have a suggestion about how to actually pull this information out of the results object? Is there a way of identifying nodes in a results object where specific state changes occur? I’m guessing it’ll be a combination of the values found in ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node and ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_bottom_below_node but I’m not entirely certain what it is that I would actually do with this.

Any advice would be appreciated.

Many Thanks,

James

messages.body_plain:
Hi -- sent this before but from wrong email. I am now traveling for a week + and may be scarce. Cheers, Nick

Hi --  it means what it says...those two things are not the same length for some reason!  Probably it is something about having accidentally or intentionally changed the include_null_range setting, the list of states, etc.

Look carefully at this part of the script:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeographical-stochastic-mapping-example-script#BSM_script
colors_list_for_states = get_colors_for_states_list_0based(areanames=areanames, states_list_0based=states_list_0based, max_range_size=max_range_size, plot_null_range=TRUE)

Use the length() function to determine the length of:

"colors_list_for_states" - the list of colors for each state (a state is a geographic range)

"states_list_0based" - the actual list of states (where each state has 0 or more areas)

See also:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!search/possible_ranges_list_txt$20colors_list_for_states/biogeobears/zkHP_YpA9kY/KKpxrdp8tC0J

Make sure you are using the script at http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeographical-stochastic-mapping-example-script#BSM_script and not some older one, make sure you're using the latest source() commands, make sure you're running the script from the top and not skipping or repeating lines through sloppy copy/paste, etc.

If you can't figure it out, email me everything, but I am traveling soon so this could take awhile.

Cheers!

messages.body_plain:
This is likely due to having changed something about the null range (0 areas).  The null range is the first range in the list of ranges/states, so if your likelihood analysis assumes the null range exists, but your graphing of the results assumes it doesn't, then everything would be shifted by 1. So, search your script on "include_null_range" and see if/where you've got this TRUE or FALSE (the defaults are TRUE, so start with that).

Cheers,
Nick

messages.subject: Re: BiogeoBears plotting question
messages.body_plain:
Hi Paul,

On Tue, Aug 29, 2017 at 12:25 AM, Paul van Els <paulv...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Nicholas,
>
> I am trying to use BioGeoBears to produce a publication-worthy illustration of my tree + reconstructed states (pie charts). However, I cannot seem to remove the boxes containing tip states at the tips. Is there a way to do this using the following function?
>
>
> plot_BioGeoBEARS_results(results_object, plotwhat="pie", tipcex=0.0, statecex=0.8, splitcex=0.0, titlecex=0.0, plotsplits=TRUE, cornercoords_loc=scriptdir, include_null_range=TRUE, tr=tr, tipranges=tipranges, label.offset=1.5)
>
> Thanks,
>
> -Paul
>

There is not a way to remove the tip states officially. I think that some people have tried tipcex=0 or tipcex=0.01 or something.  Or, you can always just edit the PDF in Adobe Illustrator or some such.

But, as I have mentioned various times on the BioGeoBEARS google group (CCed), plot_BioGeoBEARS_results is just a wrapper for the APE functions plot.phylo, tiplabels(), etc.

So if you:

1. Type plot_BioGeoBEARS_results and hit return, in R

2. Copy-paste the function code that results, copy to plot_BioGeoBEARS_results2.R or something like that

3. Look for lines with commands like "tiplabels"

4. Comment out/modify such lines to do what you want with tip labels

5. Save plot_BioGeoBEARS_results2.R  and then use the source() command on it

...you should be able to produce the behavior you want.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject_clean: Package rexpokit_0.26.1.tar.gz has been built for Windows
messages.body_plain:
Hi all BioGeoBEARS users,

A recently I submitted a bunch of updates to "rexpokit", a dependency of BioGeoBEARS that does the matrix exponentiation step using the FORTRAN library EXPOKIT.

Here is the CRAN link:

rexpokit: R Wrappers for EXPOKIT; Other Matrix Functions
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rexpokit/index.html

The FORTRAN code is fast, but old, so over the years a number of installation issues accumulated as CRAN (the Comprehensive R Archive Network) updated their code checks, standards, etc.

It was a huge pain, but I finally got the FORTRAN modernized and approved by CRAN, and now CRAN has produced executables for different operating systems, so it should install quickly on Windows etc. without dealing with any compilers etc.

This version, 0.26.1, also incorporates some improvements that were in the 0.25 version (due to Drew Schmidt at University of Tennessee, Knoxville) which was available on GitHub previously, and which should make the calculations a bit faster (Drew suggested 10%-40% faster). Thanks Drew!

Everything should work the same as before, but if you have problems getting the new version to install or notice severe weirdness after the update, please message the Google Group.  CRAN does not save the old executables, but I have saved the old versions here in case anyone needs them:

Archived executables
http://phylo.wikidot.com/rexpokit#archived_executables

Cheers,
Nick

PS: See also:

Update, August 2017: fixed many new CRAN check issues
http://phylo.wikidot.com/rexpokit#fortran_update_2017

For background and general google-ability, here are the major edits made to update the FORTRAN, and various notes that arose/error messages that were dealt with. This might help other people dealing with old FORTRAN code in R packages.
http://phylo.wikidot.com/rexpokit#fortran_update_2017

messages.subject: Sept. 26, 2017: BioGeoBEARS workshop at India biogeography meeting
messages.subject_clean: Sept. 26, 2017: BioGeoBEARS workshop at India biogeography meeting
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

For anyone attending the September 26-28 biogeography meeting in Bengaluru, India, I am giving a BioGeoBEARS workshop on September 26.  I believe the meeting organizers have sent around an email to registered meeting attendees asking for them to sign up for workshops.

I believe you can still sign up for the meeting from within India, but it may be too late international attendees, as they need a lead time on the visas. However, it might be possible, depending on the country etc.  (As a U.S. citizen in Australia my visa took about 1 week, but there is an India Visa Center right here in Canberra.)

Here are the workshops available:
https://www.biogeography.in/plenaries-workshops/

The description for the BioGeoBEARS workshop:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-workshops#India
================
Workshop Summary: Historical biogeography methods have long been dominated by the "dispersal versus vicariance" debate, and different computer programs (e.g. DIVA, Lagrange, BayArea) have made different fixed assumptions about the importance of these processes. Researchers typically just run the different programs, and observe whether or not the inferences differ, but they have no ability to judge, statistically, which of the models best fits the data, or whether another model (for example, one including founder-event speciation) might be better than any of these.

The R package BioGeoBEARS allows users to compare speciational models, as well as build more complex models (dispersal probability as a function of distance, island emergence and submergence, inclusion of fossil data). All of the models are directly comparable in the common framework of statistical model choice. Attendees of this workshop will learn how to build and test models in BioGeoBEARS, as well as necessary basic skills in R and statistical model choice.

Previous experience with R is helpful, but NOT required. Attendees may wish to bring their own phylogenies and geography data and run it at the end of the workshop.

We will cover:

Basics: historical biogeography processes and models, basic likelihood-based statistical model selection, diagramming and interpretation of results

Advanced: Biogeographical Stochastic Mapping (BSM), distance-dependent dispersal models, trait-dependent dispersal

Requirements: R experience helpful but not required - I have written a short "Intro to R" tutorial which those new to R may work through beforehand.

Equipment: Bring a laptop or share with someone (cross-plaform).

Setup: You will need to have R installed (free download). To install the necessary R packages, see the beginning of the example script: http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script
================

Cheers,
Nick
